Blocks in reading order: running head; running text (paragraph); heading "Versus I."; verse stanza; heading "Versus II."; verse stanza; heading "Idem Anglice reddita."; numbered English verse lines.

main_text.p: enim uila cum Anglica & Scotica, vel cum Hispanica, cognatione iungitur: etsi Hibernia pluribus annis Regibus Angliae subdita est, & a Scotia haud multum distat: uti nec ab Hispania; quae curis faventibus tridui navali cursu, ab occasu poteft attingi. Barbaram igitur & inconditam linguam no, infcite dixeris: ut vel ex his infra scriptis versibus Psalmi cIII. luculenter appa et.
main_text.head: Versus I.
main_text.p:
Anaim chlao'n,chcmh falfa,
molfa tighearna ar faorthe:
a uile bhriogh chorpardhe,
molvigh fos a ainm naomhtha.
main_text.head: Versus II.
main_text.p:
Mol a anuim jongla in fon
an tighearna fuaire folus:
mol a uile thiodhluice,
nar dearmuid gan a moladh, &c.
main_text.head: Idem Anglice redditi.
main_text.p:
1. My foule giue laud unto the Lord,
my spirit shall do the same:
And all the secretes of my hart
praise ye his holy name.
2. Giue thankes to God for all his gifts, shew

page.notes: The English verse lines are printed in an English type; "shew" is the catchword at the foot right. Where the scan is faint, the Irish/Gaelic stanzas are read with [?] only where doubtful. The "Giue thankes" line is partly obscured by a fold on the scan; "thanckes" read as printed. The Latin prose line "appa et." is copied as printed.
